candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — therapeutic communication, dignity and individualized psychosocial care
candidate.blueprint_topic: Communication with clients with intellectual disabilities
candidate.educational_objective: Use respectful, individualized, direct communication with an adult client who has an intellectual disability.

options.A: Communicate clearly and directly with the client, adapting the communication method as needed rather than automatically directing all questions to the family member.
options.B: Direct all communication to the family because an intellectual disability means the client cannot participate.
options.C: Use the same fixed communication method for every person with an intellectual disability.
options.D: Avoid asking the client questions because additional time for communication is not clinically useful.

candidate.rationale: CDC guidance for healthcare providers recommends effective communication with patients who have intellectual disabilities, including communicating clearly and directly with the patient, repeating or rephrasing information or using another method when needed, and taking the time required to meet the patient's healthcare needs. Therefore A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Healthcare providers should communicate effectively with patients with intellectual disabilities, communicate clearly and directly with the patient, adapt communication when needed, and allow adequate time.
candidate.source_document_title: Disability and Health Information for Healthcare Providers
candidate.source_locator: What healthcare providers can do — communicate clearly and directly with the patient; adapt wording/method if needed; take the time needed; overview explicitly includes intellectual disability
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A nurse is caring for an adult client with an intellectual disability. A family member begins answering every question for the client. Which communication approach is most appropriate?
